text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
-- SERBIA --
NASA BORBA

- Yugoslav President Zoran Lilic's term expires on Thursday. The only candidate for the post is Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic nominated by the ruling Socialist Party of Serbia. According to constitution, new president must be elected by July 25.
- Yugoslavia asked an 80 percent reduction of its $2.4 billion debt to London Club at the talks with commercial bank creditors held in London.
- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic to visit Kosovo on Wednesday.
- Montenegrin parliament to resume its session on July 1.
- Regime is trying to turn election system in its favour, says U.S. State Department on proposed law on local government.

- Vesna Pesic, leader of the Civic Alliance of Serbia, one of the coalition Zajedno members, says that only cooperation of truly democratic forces can succesfully change the difficult situation in Serbia.
- According to the draft law on local government, number of electoral units in Serbia to change to 29 from nine.
- The Democratic Party of Socialists of Montenegro seems on verge of definitive split.
- Gorica Gajevic, the general secretary of the Socialist Party of Serbia, says rightist forces are breaking up Yugoslavia.
- At the round table talks between Serbian and Kosovo Albanian representatives both sides entrenched in their old positions.
- Serbian pensioners to protest for the second time on June 26 demanding payouts of delayed payments.

- Vojislav Stanimirovic, president to the Independent Democratic Party of Serbs in Croatia, said Croatian Democratic Union not sticking to agreement. Return of refugees and displaced persons key problem in Eastern Slavonia in Croatia, he said.
- The United States halt a $30 million loan to Croatia. The move supported by Western allies.
- Outdated agricultural mechanisation to reduce wheat harvest this year by up to 140,000 tonnes.
- Analysts say some 200 million German marks sufficient to stabilise exchange rate.
- Intensive talks between Yugoslav car producer Zastava and French Peugeot continue talk on possible cooperation.
- Serbian war invalids to protest on Thursday because of state neglect and delayed payouts.
POLITIKA
- All proposals on electoral conditions by next week, said at a meeting of Serbian government and parliamentary parties.
- Serbian Privatisation Minister Milan Beko receives delegation of Royal Dutch Shell.
- Serbian Finance Minister Dusan Vlatkovic nominated for National Bank of Yugoslavia governor.

- Yugoslavia's Beobanka and Greece's Agrotiki bank sign agreement on bilingual savings account books which allows Yugoslavs to deposit U.S. dollars, German marks or Swiss francs in Yugoslavia and get drachmas in Greece.
- Yugoslav Foreign Trade Minister Borisav Vukovic says Yugoslav reintegration in the international community is a lenghty process.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- According to latest forecasts, wheat production this year will be 2.8 million tonnes, or 1.3 million tonnes more than last year, says Yugoslav Wheat Fund Director Vukosav Sakovic.
- Serbian Renewal Movement spokesman Ivan Kovacevic says opposition coalition Zajedno no longer exists.
- Deputy National Bank of Yugoslavia Bozidar Gazivoda denies rumours of free and unlimited sale of hard currency to citizens, says foreign exchange reserves raised.
- Yugoslav border guards clash with group of Albanian who tried to infiltrate Yugosalvia near Prizren; one guard wounded.
- From July 1, Yugoslavs can take $5,000 out of the coutnry for business trips.
-- MONTENEGRO --
POBJEDA
- Main board of the Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS) of Montenegro backed nomination of Slobodan Milosevic for federal president.

- Montengro should establish a recall procedure of the federal parliament members from the upper Chamber of Republics if they vote against the interest of the republic, said republic's deputy prime minsiter Miodrag Vukovic.
- Montengrin finance minister Miodrag Gomilanovic said it was not certain that Montenegrin citizens could buy German marks from the sale of Telekom Srbija. -- Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 222 4254
